# windows_directory (Data Source)

Reads the observed state of an existing directory on a remote Windows host without managing it.

Declarative attributes of the sibling resource (`ensure`, `recursive_delete`, `create_parent_directories`) are intentionally absent: the observed state is exposed read-only instead.

Returns an error when the directory does not exist on the target host.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Look up the observed state of an existing directory.
data "windows_directory" "logs" {
  path = "C:\\data\\logs"
}

output "logs_item_count" {
  value = data.windows_directory.logs.item_count
}

output "logs_last_write_time" {
  value = data.windows_directory.logs.last_write_time
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `path` (String) Absolute path of the directory on the target host. The directory must already exist.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `attributes` (List of String) Directory attributes observed on the host: hidden, readonly, system.
- `exists_children` (Boolean) True when the directory directly contains at least one file or sub-directory, as observed on the host.
- `id` (String) Data source identifier: the normalised absolute path of the directory.
- `item_count` (Number) Number of items (files and sub-directories) directly contained in the directory (non-recursive), as observed on the host.
- `last_write_time` (String) Last write timestamp of the directory, ISO 8601 UTC, as observed on the host.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
